spans.s: apakāra, m. injury. [√1kṛ + apa.]
apakārin, a. injuring. [do.]

apacāra, m. going off; absence. [√car
+ apa.]

á-patighnī, a. f. not husband-slaying.
[402: acct, 1288a.]

ápatya, n. offspring; child; young (of
animals). [ápa, ‘off,’ 1245b.]

a-pád [391], a. footless. [cf. ἄποδ-ες,
‘halt’: 1304a.]

āpad, f. misfortune. [lit. ‘a getting into’
(trouble), √pad + ā: for specialization of
mg, cf. ārti, and Eng. ac-cident, lit. ‘a happening’
(of trouble).]

apabhraṣṭa, a. fallen off; deviating (from
good grammar); provincial. [√bhraṃś +
apa.]
a-pārá, a. boundless. [pārá: acct, 1304a.]

a-parāṅmukha, a. not having an averted
face, i. e. not turning the back, 5^19.

á-parājita, a. unconquered; w. diś, the
northeast quarter, 99^23N. [√ji.]
aparādha, m. sin. [√rādh + apa.]

a-parijāta, a. not completely grown (of
an embryo), i. e. prematurely born, stillborn.
 [see pari-jāta and ref.]

a-pariṇīya, grd. without any leading
around. [√nī.]

á-parimita, a. unmeasured, unlimited.
[√1mā.]
apás, see ap.

ápas, n. work. [perhaps from √*ap, ‘reach,
take hold of’--see √āp: cf. Lat. opus,
‘work.’]
ā́pas, see áp.

apāya, m. a going away; what takes one
from the mark (cf. upāya); danger;
disadvantage; diminution. [√i + apa,
1148. 1a: for mg, cf. Eng. untoward.]
āpaṇa, m. market. [√paṇ + ā.]
